definitions.explanation: A direct, coarse word for urine or urinating. Common in everyday male speech and informal writing, but considered crude in polite contexts.

definitions.gloss: backing out; reneging on a deal (slang)
definitions.explanation: Used in expressions like {小便|しょうべん}する to mean breaking a promise, walking away from a deal, or pulling out of an arrangement. Rough, informal register.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}が{電柱|でんちゅう}に{小便|しょうべん}をした。
examples.english: The dog peed on the utility pole.

examples.japanese: ここでの{小便|しょうべん}は{禁止|きんし}されている。
{酔|よ}っ{払|ぱら}いが{道端|みちばた}で{小便|しょうべん}をしているのを{見|み}て、{眉|まゆ}をひそめた。
examples.english: I frowned when I saw a drunk man urinating on the side of the road.

examples.japanese: あいつは{土|ど}{壇場|たんば}で{小便|しょうべん}した。
examples.english: He backed out at the last minute.

examples.japanese: {大事|だいじ}な{契約|けいやく}を{小便|しょうべん}されて、{会社|かいしゃ}は{大|おお}{損|ぞん}した。
examples.english: The company took a huge loss when the other side reneged on an important contract.

examples.japanese: {口|くち}{約束|やくそく}だけで{小便|しょうべん}されるのを{何度|なんど}も{経験|けいけん}してきた。
examples.english: I've experienced people backing out on verbal-only promises many times.

notes:
Literally "small convenience," paired with {大便|だいべん} ("large convenience," feces). In polite or medical contexts, use {尿|にょう} or おしっこ instead. {小便|しょうべん} sounds rough and is more common in male speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小便|しょうべん}をする: to urinate
- {立|た}ち{小便|しょうべん}: urinating in public (a punishable minor offense)
- {小便|しょうべん}{小僧|こぞう}: "the peeing boy" — a famous statue, also a metaphor for someone immature

REGISTER:
- おしっこ: pee — childish/cute, used by children or with children
- {尿|にょう}: urine — clinical/medical
- {小用|しょうよう}: number one — softer, often used in older or polite speech
- {小便|しょうべん}: pee, piss — rough, masculine register

SENSE 2 NOTE:
"To back out" usage is slangy and rare in polite contexts; common in business gossip and rough speech.
